messages:
Nina (infra): Heads up — interruption rate on G5 spot pools in us-west1 spiked to ~8% this morning during peak. I'm prototyping an "insurance" mix: small reserved warm buffer + mixed spot pools with different allocation strategies. Thoughts?
Miguel: Can you share the metric? 8% sounds high but depends on duration. Is that preemptions per allocation or per hour?
Nina (infra): 8% of new allocations over a 30m window, median reclaim ~45s. Spike aligns with auction activity around 11:40 UTC.
Sara: Split workloads: latency-sensitive inference -> capacity-optimized pools with a modest max_bid; batch/training -> price-optimized. Keep ~10% warm buffer of pinned nodes to hide cold-start.
Trent: +1. Also set autoscaler fallback to ondemand after N failed allocation attempts. e.g., if pending pods >20 for >60s -> scale ondemand, then drain spots when ondemand is healthy.
Miguel: We should avoid blasting bids. Suggest an "insurance bump" only for critical pools: small delta over historical 95th pct price (like +10%). That reduces cost blowouts.
Nina (infra): Current ASG uses price-optimized with no max_bid (market default). I'm testing: allocation_strategy=capacity-optimized for "g5-critical" and max_bid=1.1*95pct_history for that pool.
capacity-bot: Deploy log: updated node group 'g5-critical' -> allocation_strategy=capacity-optimized, max_bid=1.1x95pct. Rolling update started. :truck:
Sara: Also mix instance types (G5/G4x) inside the pool to increase aggregate capacity and lower correlated preemptions. Add preemption handler to checkpoint long-running work to S3 within 30s.
Trent: Add soft-eviction flow: on preemption signal mark pods as "draining" and reschedule short tasks to warm buffer. TTL on warm buffer to avoid cost bloat.
Miguel: Experimental plan: A/B two strategies across regions (us-west1 & us-central1). Track interruption_rate, recovery_time, cost_per_gpu_hour, and percent_on_ondemand. Run for 7 days.
Nina (infra): I'll kick off the experiment and add dashboards. Quick pseudo-rule I'm adding to the autoscaler runbook for clarity:
```
if pending_pods > 20 and pending_time > 60s:
  - escalate -> provision_ondemand(count = ceil(pending_pods * 0.5))
  - alert #eng-oncall
  - fallback window = 10m
```
Miguel: Nice. Also log bid refunds/price spikes so finance can reconcile anomalies.
Sara: One more: add a probe that attempts a tiny higher-bid request (1-2 instances) to test capacity before scaling entire pool. Helps avoid mass reallocation failures.
Nina (infra): Good call. I'll add a probe job and start the run tonight. Thanks team :thumbsup:
